plan.downtime: ~30-90 s in two pieces: Grafana is STOPPED while its volume is tarred (seconds; longer with many plugins), started again, then recreated on the new image, whose first start migrates grafana.db before it answers. Dashboards on :3000 and alert evaluation pause meanwhile
plan.oneWayWhy: grafana.db's schema migrates on first start and cannot be downgraded
preflight: the plan is still current: recomputed from main, the running container and discovery, it has this id
free disk: at least twice (the image + the snapshot) on the backup disk and on Docker's
t-grafana is running and healthy, and its canaries pass NOW - an update is never verified against a component that was already broken
`just up-graf` would recreate t-grafana and nothing else in its compose project (compose config hashes), so no other pending change rides along
the newest backup in ~/backups/{postgres,grafana} is under 24 h old
no other update is running (one global lock)
plan.rollback: ONE-WAY: on any failure after the pull, the pre-update snapshot is restored FIRST - always, because the new version may already have migrated the data and the old one cannot read it - with the new container stopped. Then the previous image goes back on every pin line (left uncommitted) and the recipe runs again, and the old image must pass the same canaries. Anything written between the snapshot and the rollback is lost.
plan.signedOut: nobody - Grafana's sessions live in grafana.db, which the update keeps. A rollback restores the snapshot, which ends any session started after it

snapshot.what: Grafana STOPPED and its whole volume (grafana.db and plugins) tarred, grafana.db integrity-checked, then started again; plus every pin line, the compose file, this plan and the old image's id and digest
